title: Coach Sherée
description: Meet Sherée Bergman, a certified life coach, speaker, and spiritual mentor in Algonquin, Illinois, supporting emotional healing and healthier relationships.
html:
Sherée Bergman is a certified life coach, speaker, and spiritual mentor who helps people work through emotional wounds, recognize unhealthy patterns, and deepen their relationship with God. At the heart of her work is a simple conviction: no story is beyond God’s redemption, and painful experiences do not have to define the future.

Through Heart to Heart Life Coaching, Sherée combines biblical principles with practical coaching tools in a welcoming, grace-filled setting. She helps clients explore how childhood experiences, relationships with caregivers, and unresolved hurt may influence their beliefs, choices, and relationships today. Her approach encourages understanding, self-compassion, healthy boundaries, and meaningful steps toward emotional and spiritual growth.

Sherée’s commitment to this work comes from her own life. Childhood emotional neglect and family dysfunction left wounds she carried into adulthood. Her journey has included toxic relationships, chronic emotional abuse, divorce, single parenting, brain surgery, temporary blindness, and the traumatic loss of her mother. Through these experiences, her relationship with Jesus Christ became the source of healing, strength, and hope.

That journey shapes how she walks alongside others. Sherée understands the courage it takes to acknowledge painful experiences, question familiar patterns, and begin making changes. She offers space for clients to feel heard and understood while exploring the next steps in their own healing journey.

Sherée is the founder of Heart to Heart Life Coaching in the Chicagoland area. Her professional credentials include certifications in Life Coaching, Christian Life Coaching, Relationship Coaching, Relationship Communication, Grief and Joy Restoration, HeartMath Coaching, and Christian Counseling. As an ordained minister and chaplain, she brings spiritual discernment and pastoral care to her coaching, creating a holistic approach that addresses the emotional, relational, and spiritual needs of those she serves.

Her books—Start at Start to Finish Strong, Start at Start Transformation Guide, Start at Start Breakthrough Journal, and I Can’t Love You Through the Fence—explore emotional wounds, the importance of feeling safe in relationships, and restoration through faith in Christ. Through her writing, workshops, speaking engagements, and support group, she encourages people to recognize limiting beliefs, understand their responses to stress, and build healthier ways of relating to themselves and others.

Sherée lives by the promise of Romans 8:28: “And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love Him, who have been called according to His purpose” (NIV). This scripture is more than a belief—it’s the foundation of her story and the reason she can confidently guide others through their own.

Sherée lives in Algonquin, Illinois, and is the mother of three adult children. She enjoys spending time with family and friends, writing, decorating, organizing, crafting, biking, glamping, and quiet walks with her two small dogs. Her interest in dog training, shaped by years working as a surgical technician in an animal clinic, continues today as she trains her Yorkshire Terrier in agility.

Above all, Sherée treasures time spent sitting with the Lord and believes that God is the Great Healer. Her desire is to help others move forward with the assurance that their past does not disqualify them from a life of hope, connection, and purpose.

title: Orphan Wound
description: Explore the Orphan Wound, relationships with earthly fathers and our Heavenly Father, and questions for personal reflection.
html:
Did you know there is something very special and unique about the role of the father in a child’s life? The relationship between the father and the child is where our identity is formed, and it should be a healthy picture of how our Heavenly Father interacts with us.

So, when we are abandoned, rejected, abused, or just not emotionally bonded with our earthly father, a deep void is created. That void creates a mindset; we call this mindset the "Orphan Wound". It’s a matter of “trust”.

This often makes it difficult for us to interact with and have a deep intimacy with our Father in Heaven. Most of us say with our mouths that we believe in that love, but our hearts are not so sure sometimes. Truly knowing our Heavenly Father's love is critical for a Believer to function as a healthy member of the Body of Christ. Are we still saved? Of course, but a healing needs to take place so you can experience the fullness of God's promises for your life.

Ask yourself these questions:

  • Do I have a difficult time with connecting with Father God in an intimate way?
  • Do I have difficulty with emotionally connecting with my spouse? (This isn’t just for women; a man can have difficulty emotionally bonding with his wife)
  • Do I operate out of insecurity?
  • Is it hard for me to have deep relationships? Are most of my relationships at a surface level?
  • Am I jealous of or envious of others’ successes?
  • Do I struggle with abandonment, loneliness, alienation, and isolation?
  • Do I have this feeling like I'm on the outside-looking in?
  • Do I serve God to earn His love?
  • Do I tend to manipulate?
  • Do I self-medicate by pulling deeply inward?
  • Do I inwardly have some self-hatred?
  • Do I struggle with self-worth?
  • Do I fill the void by working constantly, through physical gratification or with narcissistic behavior and/or self-indulgence?
  • Do I anesthetize deep hurts with addictions, overindulge in things, etc.?
  • Am I driven by the need to succeed? Am I performance-driven?
  • Do I use people to accomplish my goals?
  • Do I repel my biological or spiritual children?
  • Do I struggle with anger or fits of rage?
  • Am I in competition with others a lot? Even silently?
  • Do I lack self-esteem?
  • Do I receive my identity from material possessions, physical appearance, or activities?

If you’ve answered yes to several of these,
it’s safe to say there may be a broken-heart issue that is in need of healing.

html:
Grief and Joy Restoration

Loss is universal but grief is personal.

Grieving is normal, however if these feelings are prolonged, they can become toxic,
​which is why we need to learn about how to relieve toxic thoughts to stay healthy, mentally, spiritually and physically.

Some examples of situations that cause loss or grief symptoms: 

Parenting as a grandparent due to unforeseen circumstances
Natural disaster (i.e. Mar., 2011 earthquake/tsunami in Japan)
Financial loss due to unscrupulous dealings
Poor or hurtful choices of one’s children
Loss or death of a beloved family pet
Death of a spouse, child, loved one
Loss of a relationship or friendship
Being overlooked for promotion
Loss of a home to foreclosure
Imprisonment of a loved one
Loss of a marriage - Divorce
Breakup of some kind
Career change
Loss of health
Loss of a job
Miscarriage
Retirement 
Abortion
and more.

who needs joy restoration coaching?
Are you stuck or having a difficult time moving forward in your life because of something that happened?
Have you lost your spouse?
Are you having difficulty forgiving someone and letting go?
Did you lose your home?
Do you lack joy and/or peace in your life?
Have you lost your job?
Do you lack motivation from a loss?
Are you fearful to move on after a divorce?
​Have you just buried a parent?
Have you experienced a break up of a meaningful relationship?

​
​These are just a "few" reasons a person may be needing a Joy Restoration Coach.  
​Especially if a person is struggling longer than they think they should.
Everyone experiences loss at sometime in their life.  
There are the normal stages a person goes through after a loss
but if you feel that you are not recovering emotionally,
​think about getting some coaching direction and support.  

You do not have to do this alone or loose months or even years from your life because of what happened.  

You don't necessarily need counseling but you may need Grief/Joy Restoration Coaching.


Remember,  you will be investing in the best possible resource – yourself!


Wouldn't be nice to be able to help others when you are on the other side of what has happened to you?

five stages of grief 

Denial and/or Isolation - The first reaction to learning of a death of a cherished loved one, a spouse who is leaving or some tragedy that just happened is to deny the reality of the situation. This is a normal reaction to the overwhelming emotions. It is a defense mechanism that buffers the immediate shocking news. We want to block out the words and hide from the facts. This is a temporary response that carries us through the first wave of pain.  We may even imagine that the former spouse, family member, friend or pet will be coming around the corner in the home for days after.

Anger - As the effects of denial begin to wear off, the reality and its pain re-emerges. It's too much to take. This intense emotion is diverted from our vulnerable core and can be expressed as anger. The anger may be aimed at objects, a spouse, strangers, friends or family….or even be directed towards our deceased loved one. We may resent the person for causing us pain. We may even feel guilty for being angry which can make us even more angry.

Bargaining - Bargaining is a normal reaction to feelings of helplessness and vulnerability.  We want to regain control of our lives and not feeling the way we feel.  We say to ourselves….if only I tried harder at the relationship….if only I went and got medial advise sooner….if only I warned them the road were really slippery.  Secretly, we may make a deal with God or our higher power in an attempt to stop or postpone the inevitable. This is a weaker line of defense to protect us from the painful reality.

Depression - There can be two levels of depression associated with mourning. Sadness, hopelessness, regret, worry are just some of the feelings that predominate depression. We worry about the costs and burial. We worry that, in our grief, we have spent less time with others that depend on us.  We may need a bit of helpful cooperation and a few kind words.  Some may experience a second level of depression which is (after the funeral, divorce, job loss, etc.) the person is not taking care of themselves such as bathing, eating, do errands and tasks, even feelings of suicide. This is the time to reach out to a counselor or grief coach.  

Acceptance - Reaching this stage of mourning is a gift.  The word gift is used because some may never see beyond the anger or depression and sadly sometimes it's by choice.  Acceptance is not just a "period of happiness".  It is not a mark of bravery and to deny ourselves the stages listed above.  This stage is about accepting the reality that our loved one is physically or relationally gone, the home or job is gone, or what ever the loss may be and recognizing that this new reality is the permanent reality.  In time, through bits and pieces of acceptance, we see it as the new norm with which we learn to live in.  Your peace and happiness is restored.
The best thing you can do is to allow yourself to feel the grief as it comes over you. 
​Resisting it only will prolong the natural process of healing.

The five stages of normal grief were first proposed by Elisabeth Kübler-Ross in her 1969 book “On Death and Dying.”

title: Why Coaching?
description: Explore emotional healing and Empowerment Coaching, including self-understanding, healthier patterns, boundaries, relationships, and faith.
html:
Before it described a profession, the word “coach” referred to a horse-drawn carriage that carried people from where they were to where they wanted to go. Emotional healing coaching follows a similar idea: offering support as you make sense of your experiences, recognize what is keeping you feeling stuck, and take meaningful steps toward healing.

Understanding what keeps you stuck

Painful experiences can influence how we see ourselves, respond to challenges, and connect with others. Sometimes, patterns we developed to protect ourselves become our “default,” even when they no longer serve us.

Our emotions can affect how we communicate, make choices, and approach relationships. When past hurts continue to shape our present responses, recognizing those connections can open the door to greater self-understanding and meaningful change.

Think of coaching as looking through the windshield while remaining aware of the rearview mirror. Your past can offer insight into the beliefs and responses shaping your life today. Understanding those connections can help you approach the road ahead with greater awareness and choice.

A welcoming space for healing and growth

Emotional healing coaching offers a compassionate, nonjudgmental space to explore your experiences and how they may be affecting your life today. You can share at your own pace, feel heard, and begin taking steps toward the changes that matter to you.

Through thoughtful questions, practical tools, and encouragement, coaching helps you explore familiar patterns, recognize your feelings and needs, and practice healthier ways of responding.

What empowerment means

Empowerment means developing the understanding, confidence, and ability to make choices that honor your needs and values. In coaching, this involves recognizing where you have choices, strengthening your voice, and taking manageable steps toward healthier ways of living and relating.

Empowerment Coaching brings this focus to your emotional healing journey, encouraging you to understand yourself with compassion while exploring the changes you want to make.

Through Empowerment Coaching, you can:

  • Understand your feelings and needs without judging yourself for having them.
  • Recognize emotional wounds and familiar patterns that may still influence your choices and relationships.
  • Reconnect with your values and examine beliefs that no longer serve you.
  • Rebuild self-trust by learning to recognize and honor your needs.
  • Strengthen boundaries and communication to support healthier relationships.
  • Deepen your relationship with God as you bring your experiences, questions, and hopes into your faith journey.
  • Take manageable steps forward with support that respects your circumstances and readiness.

The goal is to support you in creating a new default—one grounded in emotional safety, healthier relationships, and the freedom to move forward without being controlled by your past.

description: GLASS WALLS Most of us have heard of the “Glass Ceiling". Definition: an unofficially acknowledged barrier to advancement in a profession from rising…
html:
GLASS WALLS

Most of us have heard of the “Glass Ceiling". Definition: an unofficially acknowledged barrier to advancement in a profession from rising beyond a certain level in a hierarchy.

But what about “Glass Walls”? These are the personal barriers that keep us stuck—preventing us from moving forward in life, forming deep and meaningful relationships, emotionally bonding with the closest people in our lives,  achieving our dreams, or experiencing true joy. In fact, these walls can even stand between us and an intimate relationship with our Heavenly Father.

We all have these walls in some form, often built from past wounds and painful experiences. The challenge is that they can feel so normal, we may not even recognize they exist. Even if we sense their presence, we usually don’t understand how to get rid of them.  These Glass Walls can manifest in many ways—depression, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure or success, avoidance, negativity, paralysis, anxiety, self-sabotage, anger, illness, loneliness, bitterness—the list goes on.

These are not the reasons but the outcome.  

The good news? These walls can be broken. With awareness, healing, and faith, we can tear them down and step into the freedom, connection, and purpose we were meant to live.
Why do so many people struggle to experience real love—the kind of love God speaks about so often? The truth is, this is a challenge for many, both inside and outside the church. There are many reasons for this, but one of the most significant lies in our early relationships—especially with our fathers.

A father’s role in a child’s life is uniquely powerful. It is through this relationship that we first form our sense of identity, and ideally, it should reflect the way our Heavenly Father loves and interacts with us. But when a father is absent, emotionally distant, or rejecting, it creates a deep void—a wound that shapes the way we see ourselves, others, and even God. This void becomes a mindset, something we call the "Orphan Wound." At its core, this wound is about trust—or rather, the struggle to trust in love, including God's love.
​
Many of us know in our minds that God loves us, but deep down, our hearts wrestle with believing it. This struggle affects our ability to fully embrace the deep intimacy God desires to have with us. While salvation is secure, healing is necessary for us to truly walk in the fullness of God’s promises. Without it, we may find ourselves living in survival mode rather than thriving in the abundance of His love.

Emotional healing is addressing childhood/adult wounds and/or traumatic events that have happened in a persons life by going to the point of the pain.  The point of the pain will be found in all kinds of emotional hurts.  As a person is taken through the process of emotional healing, it's amazing how different they feel after. We don't believe that clinical psychology can bring wholeness.  It only teaches a person to cope with their wounded parts.  Only Jesus the creator can bring wholeness to a persons life.  
​
Physical healing requires rest, emotional healing requires work. Individuals that understand this process can walk a person down this miraculous path.  

​WARNING: Not addressing these hurts/wounds alters our thinking and life's path. 

​In very severe cases of woundedness:  A "wounded part" is a fragmentation of the core identity. There are different ranges of this from a wound that a person can't seem to get past, all the way to a person displaying multiple distinct identities, each with its own pattern of perceiving and interacting with the environment. The wounded parts or fragments hold the pain, terror, embarrassment and the shame of a traumatic event. This has been a coping mechanism to keep a person from losing all sense of reality. Depending on the severity and length in time of the traumatic event determines the depth and the number of fragmentations. Fragments can be created from a small form of rejection from an "important person".... all the way to severe abuse.  But again, Jesus is our healer and there is hope!

Some individuals that have gone through emotional healing have actually been able to cut back their medications for depression, anxiety, anger, etc. or have gotten completely off.  
​***We do not recommend anyone do this without doctors supervision.***  
Open-Heart Coaching helps many types of hurts and wounds....
such as abuse, the aftermath of a toxic relationship, the Orphan Wound, just to name a few.  
​But a VERY IMPORTANT part of our healing is forgiveness.  
We walk you through this process and why and how it frees the victim.

As a client, one of your most important rights is that of confidentiality.  Information obtained during counseling sessions will be confidential and will not be disclosed to anyone outside the counseling session without your written consent.  There are a few exceptions to enforcement of this right:
  • When the counselor has reason to believe you may be harmful to yourself or others
  • When the counselor suspects that a child is being abused or neglected
  • When the counselor receives a signed order or subpoena signed by a municipal judge ordering the release of information regarding your treatment.

THE SCRIPTURES
The Bible is the inspired and infallible Word of God.

Our God is one, but manifested in three persons - the Father, The Son, and the Holy Spirit, being coequal (Phil. 2:6).  God the Father is greater than all; the sender of the Word (Logos) and the Begetter (John 14:28, John 16:28, John 1:14).  The Son is the Word made flesh, the One Begotten, and has existed with the Father from the beginning (John 1:1, John 1:18, John 1:14).  The Holy Spirit proceeds forth from both the Father and the Son and is eternal (John 15:26).

description: Did you know there is something very special and unique about the father role in a child’s life? The relationship between the father and the child is…
html:
Did you know there is something very special and unique about the father role in a child’s life?  The relationship between the father and the child is where our identity is formed, and it should be a healthy picture of how our Heavenly Father interacts with us.  So, when we are abandoned, rejected or just not emotionally bonded with our earthly father, a deep void is created.  That void creates a mind-set, we call this mind-set the "Orphan Wound".   It’s a matter of “trust”.    This often makes it difficult for us to interact with and have a deep intimacy with our Father in Heaven. Most of us say with our mouths, we believe in that love but our hearts are not so sure sometimes.  Truly knowing our Heavenly Father's love is critically important and necessary for a Believer to function as a healthy member of the Body of Christ.  Are we still saved?  Of course, but a healing needs to take place so you can experience the fullness of God's promises for your life. ​​
Ask yourself these questions:

  • Do I have a difficult time with connecting with Father God in an intimate way?
  • Do I have difficulty with emotionally connecting with my spouse?
  • Do I operate out of insecurity?
  • Is it hard for me to have deep relationships?   Are most of my relationships at a surface level?
  • Am I jealous or envy others successes?
  • Do I struggle with abandonment, loneliness, alienation and isolation? 
  • Do I have this feeling like I'm on the outside-looking in?
  • Do I serve God to earn His love?
  • Do I have a tendency to manipulate?
  • Do I self-medicate by pulling deeply inward?
  • Do I inwardly have some self-hatred?
  • Do I struggle with self-worth?
  • Do I fill the void by working constantly, through physical gratification or with narcissistic behavior and/or self-indulgence?
  • Do I anesthetize deep hurts with addictions, over indulge in things, etc.?
  • Am I driven by the need to succeed?    Am I preformance driven?
  • Do I use people to accomplish my goals?
  • Do I repel my biological or spiritual children?
  • Do I struggle with anger or fits of rage?
  • Am I in competition with others a lot?  Even silently?
  • Do I lack self-esteem?
  • Do I receive my identity from material possessions, physical appearance, or activities?

If you’ve answered yes to several of these, it’s safe to say that maybe there is a broken-heart issue that is deeply in need of healing.

title: Phone or Virtual Coaching
description: Learn about phone and virtual coaching with Heart to Heart, including Zoom and FaceTime appointments, remote coaching benefits, and scheduling.
html:
Phone and virtual coaching offer a convenient way to receive personalized support without traveling. You can connect with your coach from home, your office, or another quiet, private place where you feel comfortable and can focus on your session.

Appointments are available by Phone, Zoom, or FaceTime. For virtual appointments, we will email you the meeting information before your scheduled session.

The Benefits of Phone vs. Virtual Coaching

Both phone and virtual appointments offer personalized coaching without traveling. The main difference is whether you prefer an audio-only conversation or seeing your coach during the session.

Phone appointments

  • Simple to join. Talk by phone without setting up a video connection.
  • Less screen time. Focus on the conversation without watching a screen.
  • Less concern about appearance. You don’t need to think about lighting, your background, or being on camera.
  • May feel more comfortable for personal conversations. Some people find it easier to speak openly without being seen.
  • Works without an internet connection. A standard phone call requires reliable phone service.

Virtual appointments — Zoom or FaceTime

  • Face-to-face connection. See your coach while talking from separate locations.
  • Visual communication. Facial expressions and gestures can add context to what is being shared.
  • A more familiar meeting experience. Video may feel closer to sitting together in person.
  • May help you feel more connected. Seeing your coach’s responses can offer reassurance during personal conversations.
  • Uses an internet connection. You’ll need a compatible device, camera, microphone, and reliable internet access.

Which is right for you? Choose the format that helps you feel most comfortable, connected, and able to focus. Both work best when you have a quiet, private place where you can speak freely without interruptions.

title: Characteristics of a Narcissist?
description: Look for these characteristics: They create a false persona as a protective barrier – like a false identity. They can be very likable - at least at first…
html:
Look for these characteristics: 
  • They create a false persona as a protective barrier – like a false identity. 
  • They can be very likable - at least at first but the closer you get to them, the more their true character traits come out.
  • They lie, are evasive, give half-truths and flat-out contradict themselves.
  • They gossip, smear and slander because the goal is to turn others against you in hope that others won't try and figure them out.
  • Lack of empathy.   
  • They have very little interest in introspection.
  • They control with playing manipulative hot and cold games.
  • They have an underlying sense of entitlement and grandiosity.
  • Some like playing the victim role to get attention or to twist the issue so they don't have to look inward to make changes in themselves.
  • Exaggerated sense of "self-importance".
  • Expect to be recognized as important to others without achievements that warrant it.  Especially in their marriage relationship.
  • They are unable to have deep heathy and happy relationships because they will not connect emotionally.
  • Constant denial of damages they inflicted – if they do admit, it's at a very minimal emotional level.  Narcissists tend to externalize blame, pinning the blame on everyone but themselves.
  • Have the inability or unwillingness to recognize the needs and feelings of others.
  • They are destructive and self-defeating in their marriages.
  • Failure to recognize others emotions, feelings and needs – especially closer relationships.  
  • Fragile self-esteem but appearing tough-minded or unemotional – except for anger.
  • They don't feel guilty or convicted for hurting others, they will just continue as normal as though nothing has happened or blame-shift..
  • They have difficulty regulating their own emotions and behavior which exacerbates the problems they cause.
  • They are known to use things to anesthetize themselves to escape the "emotional realm": drugs, alcohol, affairs, gambling, internet, sports, television, video games, pornography, etc.
  • They will control you with withholding affection.
  • Extra marital affairs are prevalent because it boosts their self-image and is noncommittal; even if they have a loving spouse.  
  • Pornography fills a fantasy relationship that they can control in their mind and there is no risk; which also can give them a fixation with masturbation because it gives them physically what they need without the burden of “emotional connection”. ​
  • They shun the ones who truly care and are trying to help them because they do not want to look and see that they have something wrong with themselves. 
  • They "perceive"truth being told to them as insults.
  • They can be very unforgiving and usually are revenge seeking.
  • Narcissists may show passion in the early stages of the relationship (love-bombing) but that soon dissipates once they feel they have your heart. At that point, they demote you. (another form of control)
  • Many times, they monopolize conversations so they are the center of attention.
  • They experience major problems adapting to change because they want to control.
  • People are things to be used for their benefit to fill the lack of emotional needs that weren’t met as a child.
  • They eventually sabotage or destroy their good/close relationships especially in marriage.
  • They often isolate themselves especially if they are being exposed.
  • They show patterns of manipulative, controlling behavior that involves both emotional abuse and emotional manipulation.
  • ​They usually have underlying depression and anxiety from neglect and/or abuse in childhood. 
  • They keep their surface relationships, so they won’t be lonely (again, another form of using).  
  • Personal relationships are usually at a surface level because this would require them to be vulnerable and that is “perceived danger”.  
  • Narcissists generalize that all are harmful and cannot be trusted.  
  • They are very defensive and self-protective.
  • They will sidestep your questions doing things to make you suddenly forget what you were asking. Narcissists can be very skilled at dodging and ducking questions they don’t want to answer. If you press them, they will then “slot” you as “unsafe” and will begin to avoid you.  
  • They often display condescending or patronizing attitudes.
  • They will appear to be your friend and keep you close to themselves (so it appears) as long as you are useful.
  • They can be giving but it will  always be from a non-emotional level (material items).
  • ​Men are more likely to be narcissistic than women. 
  • They are all about control to the extent they will push the people who genuinely care about them away so they can "feel" a level of control.  This disfunction derives from painful things happening in their childhood that they had no control over.

 
Christian perspective:
Jesus can heal.  This person must go back to childhood wounds and face them but also know that Jesus will help them change if they allow Him to.  They need very close accountability for a while to help them stay on the path of truth so they will not go back to the lies and habits they have believed in the past.  They also must stretch themselves and begin to be giving emotionally to others, especially the ones closest to themselves and not expecting a payback.  As children, the ones closest to them were the most emotionally dangerous so they have “labeled” ALL their closest relationships as dangerous.  This is a lie.
​

More understanding about Narcissism.

then I will hear from heaven and I will forgive their sin and will heal their land.

The Calling….

The first deliverance minister that I came in contact with told me that I was called to be a deliverance minister myself.  He went so far as praying over Sherée and I and anointing us with oil.  After that we started going to his training meetings.

Later an anointed prophetic couple gave a word to me, without any knowledge of my calling, saying I was called to deliverance ministry and God has given me the authority over the demonic realm but it was different than what I thought.  This couple told me that I was given the authority over principalities and powers, meaning the hierarchy of regional demonic domains.  

Sherée and I went to a conference that was held by a world famous exorcist and he picked us out of the crowd and ask us if we wanted to get a PhD in deliverance ministry. He then took us under his wing and trained us personally.  We later went to a very in-depth module training on deliverance in Arizona and this pastor prayed over Sherée and I to pass his anointing. My experience ministering along side of him for a few years, showed me that I actually was called and was to be used by God in this area.

A few years ago, I was told prophetically by a pastor that I would be the father of many which made me weep.  What this means is, I am called to disciple many others so that they can achieve their full purpose in God's kingdom.  God, over time, is continuing to expand His purposes in my own life.  Later at a conference out East, I was given another prophetic word about being the father of many, in which I was undone and weeping again when I received it.  At this same conference, I was anointed with the Baptism of Love which is the love of our Heavenly Father.  I am also called to show people their identity in Christ, God's love for them and the riches of their inheritance.  

The calling of ones life is God's choice but through man, it is recognized and confirmed....as in my case.  I did not see this for myself.  I did not think that God would choose to use me.  I didn't feel I was worthy.  It took prophesy from people....most whom I didn't know.  It also, over time, took God placing me in situations which showed me that I was anointed.  With God, when He sees a person is responsible with the gifts He's given, God subsequently will add more responsibility.  I found in my walk that it's true....He will never give us more than we can bear and God fully equips us for our call.

title: Abuse
description: ♥ Emotional Abuse slaughters the heart. ♥ Abusers are not easy to spot. They have the ability to be two different people. To the outside world, they often…
html:
♥  Emotional Abuse slaughters the heart. ♥

Abusers are not easy to spot.  They have the ability to be two different people.  To the outside world, they often appear to be kind, charming, loving and caring.  BUT when they are back in their homes, away from their public persona, they can be violent, aggressive and tormenting to their loved ones.  

By the time you realize this person is no longer who you fell in love with, you are probably enduring full-blown abuse but find it difficult to leave the relationship because you’re bound to him in so many ways. Your attachment to him is most likely based on how he used to be and this can make you incapable of seeing him for who he really is: A wolf in sheep’s clothing.

There are many types of abuse, sadly almost too many to name.  We have seen individuals that have gone through severe neglect, child abuse, financial abuse, physical abuse, sexual abuse, satanic ritual abuse, etc. but psychological abuse or also called emotional abuse, rarely gets the kind of attention that others receive.                                                                            

Heart to Heart Life Coaching recognizes that violence is rising at an alarming rate.  1 in every 4 women will be abused in their life time.  It is stated that domestic violence is the leading cause of death and injury in the United States.  There is no race, age, sexual orientation, gender, religious affiliation, educational background or socioeconomic level that domestic abuse and domestic violence does not affect.

Many times the perpetrator is a narcissist.  So what are the characteristics of a narcissist?
SUPPORT GROUP

One of the basic human rights he takes away from you is the right to be angry with him for the way he's treating you.
No matter how badly he treats you, he believes that your voice shouldn’t rise and your blood shouldn’t boil.
The privilege of anger is reserved for him alone.
When your anger does jump out of you—as it will happen to any abused woman—he is likely to try to jam it back down your throat as quickly as he can.
Then he uses your anger against you to prove what an irrational person you are.
This is what Sherée calls...."STARTING IN THE MIDDLE".
Abuse can make you feel straitjacketed.
You may develop physical or emotional reactions to swallowing your anger,
​such as depression, nightmares, emotional numbing, eating and sleeping problems, health problems, etc.
You’re too sensitive’ victims of abuse are told over and over by those whose reality depends on being insensitive.
Most women who have been in the victim role cringe when anyone tells them they are to sensitive.
In fact, sensitivity is a lovely trait and one to be cherished in any human being.

title: The Calling for Sheree
description: The Calling…. One winter day in November of 2003 at the end of my church service, the worship leader came up to me and asked me if I was going to the…
html:
The Calling….

One winter day in November of 2003 at the end of my church service, the worship leader came up to me and asked me if I was going to the meeting that was being held at another church near by.  I told him that I hadn't heard of any meeting but I had plans to go and see my youngest son who was in the hospital at the time.  After visiting with my son, I could not get "this meeting" out of my mind the worship leader spoke of.  I had no idea why either.  I wasn't at all interested at the time he told me about it...…it was probably over anyway, I thought.        

On the way home, I decided to drive by this church and to my surprise there were many cars in the parking lot.  I decided to go in.  I saw a long line of people who were waiting to speak with this couple that were standing at the front of the church.  I didn't know this couple and inquired from people standing around.  I was told that they were a very anointed prophetic couple that truly hear from the Holy Spirit.  I did not get in line, I just sat down and watched.

After there was no one else in the line, I felt a nudge to get up and talk to this couple.  (about what?... I thought.)  As I walked up to them, the woman told me that I was going to be doing what she was doing. (I had no idea what she meant)  Then the man started speaking, "I see a vision of a Christmas tree"…..with that I started to weep. (I had no idea why)  He continued…."I see the gifts under the tree, it's not about the tree, it's about the gifts.  I see you handing out the gifts and saying, Here, this gift has your name on it, God wants you to have this, it's for you". (by this time, I'm heavily weeping…still with NO understanding)  The man said he saw me in this vision handing out the gifts and telling people what they were.  He said to me, "You have a heart to let people know what their gifts are and helping them understand, grow and excel in them".  The woman added that I was also going to have a marriage ministry (I was divorced and alone at the time).  Then another gentleman standing by told me that I was going to be the mother of many. (at this point, I was undone)  How did they know my hearts' desires?  It MUST have been the Holy Spirit!  

​A few years later I was at a church that had a guest prophet.  She was up at the front of the church speaking when all of a sudden she walked right up to me and told me that the Lord is going to use me to help abused women.  She didn't know me at all and strangely enough, I was going through severe mental, emotional and spiritual abuse at that time.  I didn't look abused.  I looked very nice that day and was feeling pretty happy just being there. It MUST have been the Holy Spirit that revealed that to her!  The couple and this woman told me a lot more but I knew in my heart that was the hour that God let me know…."I'm calling you Sherée".

Since those times, I have become an Ordained Minister and Certified Life Coach, caring for peoples' hearts with small wounds from childhood to very deep wounds from abuse.  I have emotionally supported people in their life's struggles and I have helped and encouraged and coached many in their ventures. I loved every minute of it!  It is so amazing when you discover what you were created to do.  It's like "HE" lights a fire in your heart!  If you aren't aware of your gifts or calling yet, HE sometimes puts someone in your path to shed light on it!  (and then you know....that you know)  But also, HE equips us for the calling!
TYPES OF COACHING

Kevin and Sheree were married in 1991 after meeting at a High School Reunion.  After 10 years of a rocky marriage, they were divorced.  Even though they went through numerous counselors, pastors, programs, marriage seminars, ministries, etc.  They both wanted the marriage to work but it just didn't.  Why?  Because through all churches and programs….no one was teaching men how to be Christ-like in a marriage relationship.  Kevin and Sheree are just one couple that experienced the death of a marriage unfortunately because of this.  There are hundreds and maybe in reality thousands that are just like them.  

But through all this, there was still an ember there in their hearts for each other.  After years of trying, even after a divorce, the discovery was made.  This discovery changed their lives.  


What does God expect from a husband?  We have all heard the watered down sermons and maybe even a few good ones…..but did any one teach a step by step on what is truly expected?  If a man did not have good role models growing up, how is he to know what to do?  ​

title: Start at Start to Finish Strong Transformation Guide
description: Learn about Start at Start to Finish Strong Transformation Guide by Sherée Bergman.
html:
After finishing her book, she strongly encourages you to delve into the Start at Start Transformation Guide. This companion guide offers a structured and introspective journey, allowing you to thoroughly examine your own life experiences and the symptoms that may have emerged due to unmet foundational needs during your formative years. Within this book’s pages, you will be guided to explore and assess how the absence or inconsistency of essential emotional support from one or both parents has shaped your current mental and emotional well-being.

The Guide was created to help you identify these pivotal moments from your childhood and reflect deeply on how these experiences have influenced your adult life. You will be led through a series of exercises designed to uncover the roots of any lingering emotional pain, behavioral patterns, or relational challenges that stem from those early unmet needs. This process is both enlightening and healing, allowing you to confront and address the underlying issues that may have affected your life for years, possibly without your full awareness.

By engaging with the Transformation Guide, you will have the opportunity to gain valuable insights into your emotional history, uncovering the connections between your past and present self. This reflective journey is an essential step toward understanding how your early environment has contributed to your current challenges, and more importantly, it provides you with the tools to begin healing those old wounds. As you work through the exercises, you will develop a deeper understanding of your emotional landscape, empowering you to make meaningful changes in your life and fostering a renewed sense of self-compassion and resilience. This guide is not just a supplementary resource but a vital tool that can help transform how you view yourself and your past, paving the way for a more fulfilling and emotionally balanced future. Whether you are just beginning your journey of self-discovery or are already well along the path, the Start at Start Transformation Guide offers invaluable guidance and support as you seek to heal and grow.

By engaging with the Transformation Guide, you will be able to:

  1. Identify Personal Symptoms: Reflect on the personal symptoms or patterns you experience that might indicate unmet needs. These could include difficulties in self-esteem, challenges in forming healthy relationships, persistent feelings of insecurity, or emotional instability.
  2. Understand Emotional Impact: Gain insight into how specific unmet needs during childhood, such as lack of affection or recognition, may have contributed to your current emotional state. This understanding will help you connect past experiences with present behaviors and feelings.
  3. Assess Behavioral Patterns: Examine how unresolved childhood needs may have influenced your behavior and coping mechanisms. For example, you might recognize patterns of self-sabotage, struggles with setting boundaries, or reliance on unhealthy coping strategies.
  4. Discover Your Emotional Triggers: Often linked to unhealed wounds, these triggers can cause feelings of anger, sadness, fear, or anxiety that seem disproportionate to the current situation. Recognizing these triggers is an essential step toward emotional healing, as they serve as signals pointing to deeper issues. By understanding and addressing the root causes of these emotional responses, you can begin to gain control over your reactions and foster healthier relationships and emotional well-being.
  5. Explore Relationship Dynamics: Evaluate how unmet needs have affected your current relationships with others. This could include trust issues, difficulty forming secure attachments, or challenges in maintaining fulfilling connections.
  6. Healing Emotional Wounds: Step-by-Step : By inviting God into your healing journey, you can experience His love and guidance as you work through unresolved pain. The insights gained from assessments help you identify unmet childhood needs—whether it's love, security, or affirmation—that continue to affect your life. Through prayer, reflection, and a deepening relationship with the Lord, you can begin to address these wounds and fill the emotional gaps with His grace, leading to true healing and restoration.
  7. Uncovering the lies you’ve believed: These false beliefs are often formed in childhood or through past painful experiences and can deeply shape how you perceive yourself and interact with the world. This process involves identifying the specific lies that have taken root in your heart and mind, then actively challenging and dismantling them.

This book provides a structured approach to self-discovery and healing. It helps you pinpoint and understand the ways in which unmet childhood needs have influenced your current life. Through this process, you will be better equipped to address these issues, foster emotional growth, and work towards creating a more fulfilling and balanced life.

title: Start at Start to Finish Strong Breakthrough Journal
description: Explore how the Breakthrough Journal supports reflection on emotional triggers, familiar patterns, past hurts, and faith as part of your healing journey.
html:
The Breakthrough Journal is more than a place to record your thoughts or write about your day. It is a guided tool designed to help you explore what lies beneath strong emotional reactions and recognize wounds that may still be influencing your life. Its purpose is to help you move beyond describing what happened and begin understanding why an experience affected you so deeply.

Sometimes a passing comment, a change in someone’s tone, a disagreement, or a feeling of being overlooked can bring up intense emotions. You may feel hurt, afraid, angry, rejected, or overwhelmed without fully understanding why. An experience in the present can touch a painful place from the past, stirring feelings connected to earlier rejection, emotional neglect, criticism, abandonment, or unmet needs.

The Breakthrough Journal provides a structured way to pause and explore those moments with curiosity and compassion. Through guided prompts and honest reflection, you can look more closely at what happened, what you felt, what you believed in that moment, and how you responded. Rather than judging yourself for having a strong reaction, you are encouraged to consider what that reaction may be revealing about your experiences and needs.

Over time, your entries may reveal recurring themes. You might notice that certain situations consistently leave you feeling unheard, that conflict brings up fear, or that criticism leads you to question your worth. Recognizing these patterns can help you understand responses you developed to protect yourself—and consider whether those responses still serve you today.

Faith is also part of this process. The journal offers space to bring your feelings, questions, and painful experiences before God in prayer. You can reflect on the beliefs you have carried, consider them in light of biblical truth, and invite God into the places where you need comfort, wisdom, and healing.

You do not need to have every answer, revisit every painful experience, or work through everything at once. You can move at your own pace, return to a question when you feel ready, and seek support when you need it. Each entry is an opportunity to listen more closely to your heart and approach your story with honesty and compassion.

The Breakthrough Journal is intended to be a practical companion on your emotional healing journey—helping you recognize patterns, getting to the root of your hurt, and practice more intentional ways of responding. The goal is more than filling pages. It is gaining understanding that can support healing, healthier relationships, and meaningful change.

title: Open-Heart Coaching for Emotional Healing
description: Explore Open-Heart Coaching for Emotional Healing, the glass walls of protective patterns, self-trust, relationships, and faith-centered support.
html:
Understanding the “Glass Walls” Within

Most of us have heard of the “Glass Ceiling". Definition: an unofficially acknowledged barrier to advancement in a profession from rising beyond a certain level in a hierarchy.

But what about “Glass Walls”? These are the personal barriers that keep us stuck—preventing us from moving forward in life, forming deep and meaningful relationships, emotionally bonding with the closest people in our lives, achieving our dreams, or experiencing true joy. In fact, these walls can even stand between us and a deeper intimate relationship with our Heavenly Father. Not on His part but ours.

We all have these walls in some form, often built from past wounds and painful experiences. The challenge is that they can feel so normal, we may not even recognize they exist. Even if we sense their presence, we usually don’t understand how to get rid of them. These Glass Walls can manifest in many ways—depression, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure or success, avoidance, negativity, paralysis, anxiety, self-sabotage, anger, illness, loneliness, bitterness—the list goes on.

These are not the reasons, but these are the outcomes.

The good news? These walls can be broken. With awareness, healing, and faith, we can tear them down and step into the freedom, connection, and purpose we were meant to live.

When connection feels difficult - Orphan Wound

Why do so many people struggle to experience real love—the kind of love God speaks about so often? The truth is, this is a challenge for many, both inside and outside the church. There are many reasons for this, but one of the most significant lies in our early relationships—especially with our fathers.

A father’s role in a child’s life is uniquely powerful. It is through this relationship that we first form our sense of identity, and ideally, it should reflect the way our Heavenly Father loves and interacts with us. But when a father is absent, emotionally distant, abusive, or rejecting, it creates a deep void—a wound that shapes the way we see ourselves, others, and even God.

This void becomes a mindset, something we call the "Orphan Wound." At its core, this wound is about trust—or rather, the struggle to trust in love, including God's love.

Many of us know in our minds that God loves us, but deep down, our hearts wrestle with believing it. This struggle affects our ability to fully embrace the deep intimacy God desires to have with us. While salvation is secure, healing is necessary for us to truly walk in the fullness of God’s promises. Without it, we may find ourselves living in survival mode rather than thriving in the abundance of His love.

What Is Open-Heart Coaching?

Open-Heart Coaching offers faith-centered support as you explore the emotional aftermath of hurtful experiences and take meaningful steps toward healing.

Sometimes we tell ourselves, “The past is the past,” while familiar feelings and relationship patterns continue to affect us. Coaching creates room to explore those connections without pressure to revisit everything at once.

Through thoughtful questions, reflection, and practical tools, you can begin to:

  • Recognize beliefs and patterns that may be keeping you feeling stuck.
  • Understand your feelings and needs with greater compassion.
  • Strengthen boundaries and practice healthier communication.
  • Rebuild self-trust and consider different ways of responding.
  • Explore your relationship with God and bring your questions and pain into prayer.
  • Take manageable steps forward at a pace that respects your readiness.

Why “Open-Heart”?

The name reflects a willingness to gently acknowledge places in your heart that have been hurt, hidden, or guarded. It is a metaphor for honest reflection and personal growth.

Exploring painful experiences can feel vulnerable. Your coaching relationship should offer a respectful, nonjudgmental setting where you can choose what to share, ask questions, and pause when you need to. Healing does not require forcing yourself through overwhelming emotions.

Faith and the healing journey

At Heart to Heart, we believe Jesus is the Great Healer. Prayer, biblical reflection, and a growing relationship with God are central to Sherée’s approach. Her desire is to walk alongside you with encouragement as you seek understanding, healing, and healthier relationships.

Faith and professional mental-health care can work together. Coaching offers support for reflection and growth; licensed mental-health professionals provide assessment and treatment for trauma-related and other psychological conditions.

Moving forward with hope

Your experiences deserve to be acknowledged, but they do not have to define every chapter ahead. Understanding your “glass walls” can help you recognize where you have choices and begin practicing new ways of relating to yourself and others.

You do not have to have everything figured out to begin. There is room for questions, support, faith, and hope as you take your next step.
